summary: Specifies the process for selecting, confirming and recalling IAB and IESG members, including the operation of the Nominating and Recall Committees. It is a best current practice. It obsoletes RFC 2727, was updated by RFC 5078, RFC 5633, RFC 5680 and RFC 6859, and was replaced by RFC 7437.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3777 describes how the IETF selects candidates for the IAB and IESG and how those candidates are confirmed. It also sets out ways to resolve process disputes and recall a sitting member.

subtitle: The process RFC 3777 set out for choosing and confirming IAB and IESG members.

tldr.problem: The IETF needs a defined process to nominate, confirm and, if necessary, recall members of the IAB and IESG.
tldr.mechanism: A Nominating Committee reviews open positions and proposes candidates. The relevant confirming body accepts or rejects them, while a separate process handles recalls and disputes.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3777 obsoleted RFC 2727. It was later obsoleted by RFC 7437 and updated by RFC 5078, RFC 5633, RFC 5680 and RFC 6859.

sections.title: The Annual Selection Process
sections.content:
The annual process has three parts: forming the Nominating Committee, selecting candidates and confirming candidates. The process is due to finish within seven months, with a separate month available for unusual delays.

The committee reviews about half of the IAB and IESG positions each year. It may nominate an incumbent or another candidate. Deliberations about nominees and candidates are confidential.
sections.plainLanguage: Each year, the process forms a committee, selects candidates and asks the right body to confirm them. The committee reviews about half of the positions in each group.

sections.title: The Nominating Committee
sections.content:
The committee includes a chair, ten voting volunteers, liaisons and an advisor. The Internet Society President appoints the chair. The IAB and IESG each appoint a liaison, and the previous year's chair serves as an advisor.

Volunteers must have attended at least three of the last five IETF meetings. The chair selects ten volunteers at random using a method that is fair, unbiased and independently verifiable. No more than two selected volunteers may share a primary affiliation.
sections.plainLanguage: Ten volunteers chosen at random vote on candidate selection. Liaisons and advisors can contribute, but do not vote on candidate names.

sections.title: Nominations and Confirmation
sections.content:
Anyone in the IETF community may nominate a person for an open position, including themselves. A nominee must agree in writing before becoming a candidate. The committee sends one candidate for each open position to the confirming body, with information about the candidate's qualifications.

The sitting IAB confirms IESG candidates, and the Internet Society Board of Trustees confirms IAB candidates. A confirming body may accept some, all or none of the candidates and may request alternatives for rejected candidates.
sections.plainLanguage: Community members can suggest candidates, but each person must agree to be considered. A confirming body then approves or rejects the committee's candidate for each position.

sections.title: Disputes, Recalls and Confidentiality
sections.content:
A process dispute is first handled within the committee. If that fails, a written request goes to the Internet Society President, who appoints an arbiter. To request a recall, at least twenty eligible IETF community members must sign a petition.

People involved in selection, confirmation or recall must keep private information confidential unless it is explicitly approved for public release. When private information must be shared, the committee must limit what it shares and require recipients to follow the same confidentiality rules.
sections.plainLanguage: A dispute can be referred to an appointed arbiter. A recall request needs at least twenty eligible signers, and people involved must protect private candidate information.
